units.sPeakWS/cPeakWS: lifetime peak process working set MiB
units.miss: missed scheduled start periods in window
units.sCPU/cCPU,sUser/sKernel,cUser/cKernel: process CPU microseconds per verified read
units.sPrivate/cPrivate: end server/client private bytes in MiB (deadline_experiment)
units.paired_percent: 100 times (comparison / reference - 1), within each chronological round
units.stack_counts: process wall stack sample counts; stack presence includes time waiting and cannot establish executing CPU time

counter_columns: sends that polled timer twice or more

fixture.rust: allocated bounded Default, one bench route, four RX and four TX datagrams, eight dedup rows, four Observe entries, one receive body and two send bodies rounded to whole KiB, four Call entries, zero deferred entries and 2049 bytes of receive scratch
fixture.libcoap: stock library, dynamic PDU allocation; unprotected public separate-CON fixture and established OSCORE stock encryption allocation
fixture.comparison: single outstanding CON read, same verifying client, 32 warmups, same four packets per 1024-byte block
fixture.schedule: permutations of coaptic, trial, libcoap in lexical input order; alternate forward and reverse workload order between rounds

sampler_scope_audit.evidence: The published C, original-project and complete-control off runners have separate entry points from the profile scripts. The C and historical launcher uses distinct Python child processes. The primary off runner waits for the final profile artifact. Static source audit found no injection of the local sampler in those timing scripts. Earlier windows did not record per-window child process allowlists.

discarded.reason: The profile phase left the stack sampler installed in the original Python worker. Those runs are excluded from every performance estimate.
